events.title: CVE-2026-111917 — Vikunja 2.3.0 before 2.7.0 contains an improper session validation vulnerability that allows attackers to keep WebSocket access after revoca
events.summary: A high-severity flaw in Vikunja versions 2.3.0 through before 2.7.0 allows an attacker with a stolen access token to continue receiving a victim's real-time WebSocket notifications even after the victim's session is revoked or TOTP is enabled. The vulnerability stems from the server not checking the JWT session identifier against the sessions table when handling WebSocket connections.
events.why_it_matters: The vulnerability defeats a key security control: session revocation and TOTP enrollment do not stop an attacker from continuing to pull real-time updates containing comment, task, and project content. With a CVSS score of 7.1 and official high severity, organisations using affected Vikunja versions should treat stolen tokens as a persistent data exposure risk and prioritise patching to 2.7.0 or later.

events.title: CVE-2026-111921 — Vikunja 0.13.0 before 2.7.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows project members with Write permission to delete ad
events.summary: The project management tool Vikunja has an authorization flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-111921, in which users holding only Write permission on a project can delete admin-tier link shares. This works because the delete permission check reads a share object that has not been loaded, and attackers can enumerate sequential share IDs via DELETE requests to the projects shares endpoints.
events.why_it_matters: The vendor-assigned CVSS is 5.3 (medium), and the flaw allows low-privileged collaborators to revoke admin share links and invalidate active share sessions. It is not listed in KEV and EPSS is very low, suggesting limited observed risk so far. Defenders running affected Vikunja versions (0.13.0 before 2.7.0) should prioritise patching to prevent permission bypasses on shared projects.

claims.text: CVE-2026-111921 is rated 5.3 (medium) under CVSS 4.0 by the CNA that assigned it.
FIRST's EPSS puts the chance of CVE-2026-111921 being exploited in the next 30 days at under 1%.
A fix for code.vikunja.io/api (Go) is published in 2.7.0, per GHSA-fmmf-xq98-g327.

events.title: CVE-2026-111920 — Vikunja 2.6.0 contains a broken access control flaw in getProjectAccessForUser (pkg/models/project_access.go), which resolves a user's effec
events.summary: The open-source task manager Vikunja 2.6.0 has a broken access control bug in its project permission logic: effective rights on a child project are computed as the maximum across the project tree, so someone with write access to a parent can edit a sub-project even if they were given read-only access to it. The issue is tracked as CVE-2026-111920 and is described as contained.
events.why_it_matters: Teams relying on per-sub-project permission restrictions in Vikunja cannot assume those limits hold, since parent-project write access silently overrides them. The flaw carries a medium CVSS score of 5.3, is not listed in KEV, and has a very low EPSS estimate, suggesting limited immediate exploitation risk.

events.title: [MEDIUM] CVE-2026-111918 — Vikunja from 1.0.0-rc0 before 2.7.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in RecalculateTaskPositions that allows authenticated u
events.summary: A medium-severity authorization flaw in Vikunja versions from 1.0.0-rc0 through 2.7.0 lets authenticated users without access to any projects write task position data for all tasks on an instance, and abuse saved filters to persist cross-tenant references and amplify writes toward denial of service.
events.why_it_matters: Any shared Vikunja deployment is exposed to cross-tenant tampering and denial of service by ordinary authenticated users, with a CVSS of 5.3 from the CNA. The issue is not listed in KEV and has a very low EPSS score, and it is fixed in version 2.7.0. Defenders running Vikunja should treat upgrades as routine but worthwhile, prioritising multi-tenant instances.
